query: 人工标注在智慧情报服务 benchmark 中应优先覆盖哪些维度？
effective_search_query: 人工标注 智慧情报服务 benchmark 维度 优先级

major_issues: 报告将文献[6]中关于生成式人工智能赋能课堂教学的形态层级框架直接推广为智慧情报服务benchmark中人工标注应优先覆盖的维度，存在过度推断。证据[6]明确限定其框架应用于‘生成式人工智能赋能课堂教学’，并未声明适用于智慧情报服务benchmark。报告结论缺乏直接证据支持其跨领域适用性。
报告在‘核心主题与证据’和‘谨慎结论’部分，将其他文献（[1][2][3][4][5][7][8]）中关于智能体评估的通用挑战或关注点（如生态效度、决策偏见、利用领域知识）直接关联或推论为‘可能隐含了需要人工标注进行衡量的维度’或‘间接提示’标注设计需关注这些方面。这些关联是报告作者的推断，而非证据原文的明确主张。证据本身并未讨论这些方面与‘人工标注维度’的关联。
报告标题和核心结论声称回答了‘应优先覆盖哪些维度’的问题，但所依赖的唯一直接证据[6]来自不同领域（教育），且其他支持性关联均为推断。因此，报告的结论超出了现有摘要证据所能支持的范围，整体论证的有效性存疑。
citation_issues: 对证据[6]的引用不准确。报告称该框架‘对智慧情报服务基准测试具有参考价值’、‘为…提供了有价值的参考’，这是报告作者的评价和推断。证据[6]的摘要并未提及‘智慧情报服务’或‘benchmark’，也未就其框架在其他领域的适用性做出任何声明。引用应严格限于证据[6]所陈述的内容：该框架是针对‘生成式人工智能赋能课堂教学’提出的。
对证据[2][3][4][5][7][8]的引用存在过度解读。这些证据分别讨论了基准测试的权衡、决策偏见评估、智能体行业应用、现实挑战、知识管理框架和领域知识利用的局限性。然而，它们的摘要均未提及‘人工标注’（human annotation）或其应覆盖的维度。报告将这些内容作为支持‘人工标注维度’的‘侧面揭示’或‘启示’，建立了证据本身并未建立的关联。
revision_instructions: 重写报告结论部分，使其严格基于证据。明确指出：根据提供的摘要证据，仅证据[6]直接提出了一个关于人工标注优先维度的具体框架（四个递进维度），但该框架明确针对‘生成式人工智能赋能课堂教学’场景。其他证据均未直接讨论智慧情报服务benchmark中的人工标注维度问题。
删除或大幅修改‘核心主题与证据’第二部分中关于其他文献‘侧面揭示’或‘隐含’标注维度的论述。可以改为客观陈述这些文献关注的智能体评估的不同方面（如[2]关注评估方法权衡，[3]关注决策偏见等），但同时必须明确指出，这些摘要并未将这些方面与‘人工标注的维度’联系起来。避免做出推断性关联。
在报告的局限性和结论中，强调基于当前摘要证据，无法对‘智慧情报服务benchmark中人工标注应优先覆盖哪些维度’这一问题得出跨领域的、确定的结论。证据[6]的发现局限于教育领域，其普适性需要进一步验证。其他证据提供了智能体评估的背景，但未直接解答该研究问题。
调整报告标题和语气，以更准确地反映摘要级证据的局限性。例如，标题可改为‘教育领域生成式AI赋能形态中的人工标注维度：基于摘要的初步发现及其对智慧情报服务的潜在启示’。全文应避免将特定领域的发现表述为通用答案。

top_papers.title: Agent-Diff: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Enterprise API Tasks via Code Execution with State-Diff-Based Evaluation
top_papers.abstract: We present Agent-Diff, a novel benchmarking framework for evaluating agentic Large Language Models (LLMs) on real-world productivity software API tasks via code execution. Agentic LLM performance varies due to differences in models, external tool access, prompt structures, and agentic frameworks. Benchmarks must make fundamental trade-offs between a sandboxed approach that controls for variation in software environments and more ecologically valid approaches employing real services. top_papers.title: AIM-Bench: Evaluating Decision-making Biases of Agentic LLM as Inventory Manager
top_papers.abstract: Recent advances in mathematical reasoning and the long-term planning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) have precipitated the development of agents, which are being increasingly leveraged in business operations processes. Decision models to optimize inventory levels are one of the core elements of operations management. However, the capabilities of the LLM agent in making inventory decisions in uncertain contexts, as well as the decision-making biases (e.g. framing effect, etc.) of the agent, remain largely unexplored. This prompts concerns regarding the capacity of LLM agents to effectively address real-world problems, as well as the potential implications of biases that may be present. top_papers.title: AGENTiGraph: A Multi-Agent Knowledge Graph Framework for Interactive, Domain-Specific LLM Chatbots
top_papers.abstract: AGENTiGraph is a user-friendly, agent-driven system that enables intuitive interaction and management of domain-specific data through the manipulation of knowledge graphs in natural language. It gives non-technical users a complete, visual solution to incrementally build and refine their knowledge bases, allowing multi-round dialogues and dynamic updates without specialized query languages. The flexible design of AGENTiGraph, including intent classification, task planning, and automatic knowledge integration, ensures seamless reasoning between diverse tasks. top_papers.title: SOP-Agent: Empower General Purpose AI Agent with Domain-Specific SOPs
top_papers.abstract: Despite significant advancements in general-purpose AI agents, several challenges still hinder their practical application in real-world scenarios. First, the limited planning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLM) restrict AI agents from effectively solving complex tasks that require long-horizon planning. Second, general-purpose AI agents struggle to efficiently utilize domain-specific knowledge and human expertise. In this paper, we introduce the Standard Operational Procedure-guided Agent (SOP-agent), a novel framework for constructing domain-specific agents through pseudocode-style Standard Operational Procedures (SOPs) written in natural language.
